lead.event: MSCI’s Indonesia reclassification consultation sparks market selloff and official responses
lead.headline: MSCI proposes standalone status for Indonesia as IHSG falls 11.57%
lead.blurb: The proposal is not final, and Indonesia remains classified as an Emerging Market during consultation. If approved, Indonesian securities would leave MSCI’s Emerging Market index family. MSCI cited concerns over investability, ownership transparency and market functioning, while BEI and OJK said they would seek clarification and use the period to demonstrate reforms. Feedback is open until 30 April 2027, with a decision due by 30 June 2027 at the latest.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: BNI provides data-center financing to MGLV
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BNI provides MGLV with Rp10.75 trillion in data-center financing
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: NexAI will use the facility to fund the acquisition and development of a data center in Jababeka and construction of one in Batang. It runs for up to six years at a floating rate of 90-day compounded IndONIA plus 1.9%.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: Bank Syariah Indonesia plans its Phase II rights issue
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BRIS plans Phase II rights issue of up to 6.8 billion shares
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: Bank Syariah Indonesia will use net proceeds for financing and growth. The Rp500 nominal-value shares could raise up to Rp3.4 trillion, while the exercise price remains unset and non-participants may face dilution of up to about 12.85%. Shareholders vote on 6 November, with completion targeted for Q1 2027 subject to regulatory approval.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: BTPN Syariah shareholders approve a share buyback
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: BTPS shareholders approve Rp1 trillion share buyback
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The repurchase can cover up to 10% of issued shares, with the budget including broker fees and other transaction costs. The board can set the price under applicable regulations and must complete the buyback within 12 months of the 13 October EGM. No schedule or price has been detailed.

deals_control.event: Bayan Resources ownership transactions involving Low Tuck Kwong and Haji Isam
deals_control.headline: BYAN deal with Haji Isam remains conditional as Low sells 650 million shares
deals_control.blurb: Low sold the shares on 15 October at Rp2,588 each, leaving him with an 8.30% stake in Bayan Resources; the buyer was not disclosed. Low and Elaine had agreed to sell a combined 30.25% stake to Jhonlin Baratama for about Rp26.10 trillion at the same price, but the latest report said the agreement remained conditional. Low said he remained BYAN’s controller.

deals_control.event: Buana Lintas Lautan acquires FPSO and FSO facilities
deals_control.headline: BULL acquires US$150 million FPSO and FSO facilities
deals_control.blurb: The FPSO has a US$120 million contract through 2030, with a possible extension of up to 10 years. The FSO has a 10-year, US$50 million contract and is expected to generate US$35 million in annual income. UOB Kay Hian said the acquisition should stabilize net profit, with delivery scheduled for October 2026.

deals_control.event: Wibowo Group Capital completes its mandatory tender offer for Mitrabahtera shares
deals_control.headline: WGC completes MBSS tender offer for Rp387.22 billion
deals_control.blurb: Wibowo Group Capital acquired 132.84 million Mitrabahtera shares at Rp2,915 each, with payment made on 15 October. Its stake rose to 90.09% from 82.50%.

market_structure_policy.event: OJK sanctions DSSA, BREN, and CUAN for capital-market violations
market_structure_policy.headline: OJK fines DSSA, BREN and CUAN Rp2.1 trillion for capital-market violations
market_structure_policy.blurb: Dian Swastatika Sentosa received Rp1.5 trillion, Barito Renewables Energy Rp500 billion and Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Rp100 billion. OJK found manipulation in DSSA trading and pre-arranged offering allocations at BREN and CUAN to parties linked to controlling shareholders. All three shares hit the lower price limit after the fines.

market_structure_policy.event: PT Champion Pacific Indonesia requests voluntary delisting
market_structure_policy.headline: IGAR requests voluntary delisting as trading suspension begins 16 October
market_structure_policy.blurb: Champion Pacific Indonesia filed its request with IDX and OJK on 15 October, seeking to move from listed-public to private status. President Director Masanobu Ojima cited long-term development, operational efficiency and greater flexibility, saying the shares are not actively traded and the company has no plans to raise equity funding.

earnings_guidance.event: ANTAM reports gains from downstream expansion
earnings_guidance.headline: ANTAM reports Rp257.6 billion profit from downstream expansion
earnings_guidance.blurb: The operating SGAR refinery, managed by Borneo Alumina Indonesia, a joint venture between ANTAM and Inalum, sold 350,000 tons of alumina in semester I-2026. It targets 700,000 tons by year-end, with phase I capacity of 1 million tons a year.

earnings_guidance.event: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas raises Bukit Asam’s target price
earnings_guidance.headline: BRI Danareksa raises PTBA target price, citing 10% dividend yield potential
earnings_guidance.blurb: Bukit Asam’s revised coal-price assumptions lift 2026 and 2027 net profit forecasts by 53.9% and 51.3% to Rp5.4 trillion and Rp4.4 trillion, respectively. Analysts still expect 2027 profit to fall 18% year on year as coal prices and margins normalize.

earnings_guidance.event: Darma Henwa reports nine-month profit growth
earnings_guidance.headline: DEWA reports 114.5% growth in nine-month net profit
earnings_guidance.blurb: Net profit attributable to parent owners reached Rp513.08 billion for the nine months ended 30 September, up from Rp239.14 billion a year earlier. Revenue rose 9.6% to Rp5.1 trillion, while gross profit increased to Rp1.03 trillion.

earnings_guidance.headline: Analysts project SMGR 2026 net profit to rise 164.4% to Rp505 billion
earnings_guidance.blurb: Semen Indonesia is also forecast to post Rp38.27 trillion in revenue, up 8.57% from 2025. CGS International Sekuritas Indonesia, Binaartha Sekuritas and OCBC Sekuritas recommend add or buy, with target prices of Rp2,500, Rp2,680 and Rp2,200 per share, respectively.
